notes.text:
This update for gimp fixes the following issues:

- CVE-2026-82328: undersized palette memory allocations in the ICO loader can cause heap out-of-bounds reads
  (bsc#1277618).
- CVE-2026-82343: improper channel-count handling in the PSD loader can cause heap and stack out-of-bounds reads
  (bsc#1277622).
- CVE-2026-106061: integer overflow in the X cursor thumbnail loader leads to out-of-bounds read and process crash when
  generating a thumbnail for a crafted XMC file (bsc#1284473).
- CVE-2026-106062: heap-based buffer overflow in DirectDraw Surface loader when loading a crafted DDS image
  (bsc#1284474).
- CVE-2026-106063: heap-based buffer overflow in the DICOM export plug-in when exporting an image with extremely large
  width and height (bsc#1284475).

notes.text: A flaw was found in GIMP's X cursor (XMC) thumbnail loader. When GIMP generates a thumbnail for a crafted XMC file, it allocates a pixel buffer using a width * height size computed in 32-bit signed arithmetic. If that product overflows, the allocation is smaller than the true image extent. A subsequent GEGL buffer read uses the unwrapped dimensions and performs an out-of-bounds read on the heap, after integer overflow in the size calculation. This can crash GIMP or corrupt process memory.

notes.text: A heap-based buffer overflow was found in GIMP's DirectDraw Surface (DDS) loader. When loading a crafted DDS image, buffer sizes derived from width, height, and pitch can be computed using 32-bit arithmetic that overflows. The allocated buffer is too small for the amount of pixel data written through GEGL, following integer overflow in size calculations. This may allow heap corruption and, in the worst case, arbitrary code execution in the context of the GIMP process.

This issue can result in an application crash, leading to a denial of service or a limited information disclosure of heap memory contents.
